The story is told strictly from a close third-person perspective limited to the protagonist, Ilse. It does not dive into the mindsets, motivations, or beliefs of any other characters to provide diverse viewpoints. While the man from Lüneburg acts as a mildly antagonistic or unwelcome presence (implied to be an inspector or evaluator assessing the aging ferry), we only ever see him from the outside through Ilse's and Petersen's observations, rather than experiencing his perspective from within.
